# Ruby Gillis

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c15 P66](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0066), [v1 c26 P5](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0005), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006)</sub>
- **Status:** deceased  <sub>[v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c25 P25](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0025), [v3 c14 P37](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0037)</sub>
- **Role:** Teacher  <sub>[v1 c37 P34](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0034), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Ruby was a handsome girl with long yellow hair, bright blue eyes, and a brilliant complexion with a plump, showy figure. Her beauty was vivid and striking, and she was considered the handsomest girl of her year at Queen's Academy. Prior to her death from consumption, she grew extremely thin and pale with hectically brilliant cheeks and translucent hands.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005), [v3 c14 P31](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0031)_

## Personality

Ruby was bright, cheerful, good-tempered, and loved to enjoy the pleasant things of life. She was inclined to be hysterical and easily panicked when startled or overwhelmed. Possessing a sentimental and frivolous nature, she spent much of her time talking and thinking about boys, suitors, and romance. Beneath her shallow, gaiety-filled exterior, she harbored a deep love for babies and desperately wanted to live, marry, and have a family.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v1 c23 P16](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0016), [v1 c26 P6](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0006), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c4 P71](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0071), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)_

## History

Ruby attended Avonlea School, where she studied alongside Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Jane Andrews. As a student, she joined the Queen's Academy preparation class and later moved to Charlottetown to attend Queen's, where she was recognized as the handsomest girl of her year. After graduating with her teacher's license, she took a teaching position at Carmody, though she returned home to Avonlea on weekends. She had a wide circle of suitors and enjoyed a lively social life. After contracting a severe lung infection during a winter term, she developed galloping consumption, forcing her to give up her teaching plans for the White Sands school. During her final summer, she spent many quiet evenings talking with Anne Shirley in the Gillis garden, expressing her deep fear of death and her longing for a long life with her loved one, Herb Spencer. She passed away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter, leaving behind an unfinished piece of embroidery for Anne.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c37 P34](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0034), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c11 P8](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0008), [v3 c14 P0](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0000), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030), [v3 c14 P33](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0033)_

## Quotes

> I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright.  <sub>[v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001)</sub>

> Me! Why, I’m perfectly well. I never felt better in my life. Of course, that congestion last winter pulled me down a little. But just see my color. I don’t look much like an invalid, I’m sure.  <sub>[v3 c11 P57](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0057)</sub>

> Anne, it won’t be long now before I’ll be lying over there. You and Diana and all the rest will be going about, full of life—and I’ll be there—in the old graveyard—dead!  <sub>[v3 c14 P7](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0007)</sub>

> I don’t want to die. I’m afraid to die.  <sub>[v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011)</sub>

> I want to live. I want to live like other girls. I—I want to be married, Anne—and—and—have little children. You know I always loved babies, Anne. I couldn’t say this to any one but you. I know you understand. And then poor Herb—he—he loves me and I love him, Anne. The others meant nothing to me, but he does—and if I could live I would be his wife and be so happy. Oh, Anne, it’s hard.  <sub>[v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>
